findings.evidence: `Conformal.lean:84-97`: `suffices h : mfderiv I I (toWithMetric (g.rescale f hf hf_pos)) x c = mgradient … by rw [← h, mfderiv_ofWithMetric_mfderiv_toWithMetric]; rw [eq_mgradient_iff]; … inner_rescale …`, which has the same structure as the new lines 61-73. `Gradient/Basic.lean:72`: `rieszDual x (mvfderiv I f x)`.
findings.fix: Keep the covector lemma and reprove `mfderiv_ofWithMetric_mgradient_rescale` from it: rewrite with `mgradient_def`, identify `mvfderiv I (u ∘ ofWithMetric) (toWithMetric _ x)` with `(mvfderiv I u x).comp (mfderiv I I ofWithMetric _)` using `ContinuousLinearMap.ext` and `mvfderiv_comp_ofWithMetric_apply` (`WithMetric.lean:330`), then apply the new lemma. Placing the covector lemma before the gradient lemma, in `Riemannian/Conformal.lean` or in a module it imports, removes the repeated proof.
findings.issue: `mfderiv_ofWithMetric_rieszDual_rescale` repeats the proof of `TauCeti.WithMetric.mfderiv_ofWithMetric_mgradient_rescale` (`Riemannian/Conformal.lean:77-97`): `suffices` via `mfderiv_ofWithMetric_mfderiv_toWithMetric`, then `eq_rieszDual_iff_inner_eq`/`eq_mgradient_iff`, then `inner_rescale`. The gradient lemma is the special case φ = `mvfderiv I u x`, since `mgradient I f x = rieszDual x (mvfderiv I f x)` (`Gradient/Basic.lean:71-72`). That leaves two parallel proofs of one law.

findings.evidence: `Conformal.lean:102-110`: `inner_mgradient_rescale` is proved directly by `rw [inner_rescale, mfderiv_ofWithMetric_mgradient_rescale, …]; field_simp`, independent of the new pairing lemma.
findings.fix: Derive `inner_mgradient_rescale` from `apply_rieszDual_rescale` using `inner_rieszDual`/`mgradient_def` and the `mvfderiv_comp_ofWithMetric_apply` identification above, so the inverse-metric law has one proof.
findings.issue: Same duplication for the pairing law: `inner_mgradient_rescale` (`Riemannian/Conformal.lean:102`) is `apply_rieszDual_rescale` for differentials, because ⟪φ♯, ψ♯⟫ = φ(ψ♯) by `inner_rieszDual`. Both laws are kept with separate `field_simp`/`rw` proofs.

summary: The new covector index-raising and pairing laws are the general forms of the existing gradient laws in `Riemannian/Conformal.lean`, and their proofs repeat the same steps instead of making the gradient laws corollaries. The norm and inverse-Gram results are new.
